items.title: Brampton Man Faces Nine Charges After Three-Month Street Racing Investigation
items.summary: A Brampton man is facing nine charges following a three-month investigation into illegal street racing across Mississauga and Toronto. According to insauga.com, Peel Regional Police's Safer Roads Team identified a driver allegedly taking part in multiple illegal races while driving a vehicle with no licence plates and disguising his identity with a ski mask. The outlet reported officers spotted the same vehicle racing on two separate occasions on Sept. 26, once near Meadowpine Boulevard and Danbro Crescent, where police say the car ran a red light at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Highway 401, and again near Clayson Road and Bartor Road in Toronto. Police identified the driver as Tarman Toor, 24, of Brampton, insauga.com said. Officers executed a search warrant at a Brampton home on Oct. 28 and arrested Toor, according to the outlet. He is charged with three counts each of dangerous operation of a vehicle, disguise with intent and racing a motor vehicle, and is scheduled to appear in court in Brampton at a later date, insauga.com reported.

items.title: Ninth Line Construction Advances as Mississauga Adds Bike Lanes, Sidewalks to Growing Corridor
items.summary: Crews are well underway on a major widening of Ninth Line between Eglinton Avenue and Derry Road, a stretch that has seen heavy residential growth in recent years. According to Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden, the project will turn the former rural road into a larger thoroughfare with two travel lanes in each direction, raised medians or centre turning lanes, protected cycling tracks and sidewalks on both sides. McFadden said in a recent website update that crews have completed curb work between Eglinton Avenue and Britannia Road, with most of the sidewalk and concrete work substantially finished. Temporary traffic and pedestrian signals have already been activated at several intersections along the corridor, including Eglinton Avenue, Burdette Terrace, Henrietta Drive, Thomas Street, Erin Centre Boulevard and Britannia Road, she said. Bus pads at Skyview Street and Erin Centre Boulevard have also been completed, according to the update. Beyond easing vehicle traffic for the area's growing population, McFadden said the upgrades are meant to give cyclists and pedestrians safer options while leaving room for future public transit service.

items.title: Toronto Police Say Etobicoke Shooting Marks City's 33rd Homicide of 2026
items.summary: An 18-year-old from Mississauga has been identified as the victim of a fatal shooting in Etobicoke on Saturday afternoon, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that officers responding to the scene found a man who had been shot, and paramedics performed life-saving measures before taking him to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Police say the suspect or suspects fled before officers arrived, insauga.com said. Toronto police have identified the victim as Malik Abass, 18, of Mississauga, and released his photo, according to the outlet. The Toronto Police Service's Homicide and Missing Persons Unit is investigating, and police have not released a suspect description or said what led to the shooting, insauga.com reported. The outlet noted the shooting took place in central Etobicoke, close to the Mississauga border, and that police say it is Toronto's 33rd homicide of 2026.

items.title: Sheridan College Opens Hazel McCallion Campus Doors to Prospective Students Thursday
items.summary: Prospective college students will get a chance to tour classrooms, meet instructors and explore program options when Sheridan College hosts an open house at its Mississauga campus later this week. According to insauga.com, the event takes place Thursday, Nov. 12, at Sheridan's Hazel McCallion Campus. The outlet reported that visitors will be able to walk through classrooms, labs and student spaces, and connect with faculty and current students during interactive sessions covering individual programs and career paths. Representatives will also be on hand to discuss financial assistance options including OSAP, scholarships, bursaries, awards and work-study opportunities, insauga.com said. The outlet noted prospective students can learn about support services through Sheridan's Student Affairs department, such as health and wellness, housing, accessible learning, tutoring and advising. Because Sheridan operates three campuses in the region with different program offerings, the college is encouraging prospective students to attend the open house at the campus where their preferred program is taught, according to insauga.com.

items.title: Brampton Bans Nearly All Fireworks While Mississauga Allows One Night for Diwali
items.summary: Fireworks rules vary widely across the GTA as families celebrate Diwali, with some cities permitting a single night of use and others banning the practice outright. According to insauga.com, Toronto Fire Services reminded residents on Sunday that fireworks are not permitted on balconies, beaches, streets, parking lots or in parks, and urged people to confirm local rules before lighting them. The outlet reported that Mississauga allows fireworks without a permit on one night during Diwali, while Brampton bans the use, sale and possession of all fireworks except sparklers. In Brampton, discharging or possessing fireworks without a permit carries a $500 fine and selling them brings a $1,000 fine, with the city able to issue a court summons carrying penalties up to $100,000, insauga.com said. Property owners in Brampton can also be charged if fireworks are set off on their land, according to the outlet. The outlet noted Brampton will have extra bylaw officers on duty after receiving a record 432 fireworks complaints during last year's Diwali, and the city instead hosts its own fireworks displays at Diwali events.

items.title: Durham Health Officials Trace New Measles Exposure Sites to Pearson Airport Travellers
items.summary: Travellers who passed through Toronto Pearson International Airport last week may have been exposed to measles, according to Durham Region health officials. The Durham Region Health Department said it identified additional public exposure sites linked to a confirmed measles case in an unimmunized child from the region who had recently travelled internationally. The department said anyone who was at the identified locations should watch for symptoms until Nov. 24, and that it has already followed up directly with known contacts in Durham Region. Health officials are advising people who may have been exposed to confirm they and their families have had two doses of the measles vaccine, noting those born before 1970 likely had measles as children and are considered protected. Anyone who develops symptoms is urged to stay home from work or school, call ahead before visiting a clinic or doctor and wear a well-fitting mask when seeking care, the health department said. Officials noted measles is highly contagious, can linger in the air or on surfaces for up to two hours, and typically produces symptoms such as fever, cough, red watery eyes and a rash within seven to 21 days of infection.

items.title: Streetsville Barbershop Owner Turns Walls Into Gallery for Local Artists and His Own Paintings
items.summary: A Streetsville barbershop called Heartbreak Hotel has become more than a place for haircuts, doubling as a showcase for local art and streetwear. According to the Toronto Star, owner Omar Preza, 44, was born in El Salvador and raised in Canada, and built the shop around his lifelong passions for drawing, comic books and street graffiti. The newspaper reported that customers walk in to upbeat Latin and hip-hop music, with painted canvases in thrifted gold frames and custom apparel hanging from industrial pipe racks against black-and-white brick walls. The Star said Heartbreak Hotel began in 2013 as a streetwear clothing brand, with Preza starting to paint around the same time, and today he sells both his original fine art and custom-designed apparel in the shop alongside the haircuts. His work was included in the Art Gallery of Mississauga's 2024-2025 Fourth Annual Juried Show of Visual Arts, according to the paper.
